newsitem.title: USA: Voters approve $550 mln West Virginia road GOs.
newsitem.headline: Voters approve $550 mln West Virginia road GOs.

text.p: West Virginians overwhelmingly passed a $550 million general obligation bond issue to build and improve roads, Mary Ratliff, deputy secretary of state said Wednesday.
With 65 percent of the precincts reporting, the vote was 72 percent in favor of the bonds, Ratliff said, with 219,425 West Virginians voting yes and 86,786 voters opposed.
Final results will not be availabe until late Wednesday, Ratliff said.

The exact use of the proceeds was left vague, and that was controversial, Ratliff said. But she said the funds would be used to build and improve roads including finishing a strech of road called corridor H.

The bonds required a constitutional amendment which authorizes five annual issues of $110 million beginning in July 1997. Maturities are not to exceed 25 years. If all the bonds are not issued in a given year, the balance can be carried forward to the next year.

The proposal authorizes the state legislature to levy sufficient taxes to pay principal and interest in the bonds if money set aside in the state road fund is not enough. It does not specify the type of tax.
